title: Span Accounting — Captain's Log 2028-02-14
content:
Purpose:
A short, operational capture of the week for span accounting, sampling experiments, and dashboard changes — intended for quick handoff across on-call and infra teams. This is a working note: decisions flagged for review and a few TODOs left intentionally rough.

High-level summary:
- Experiment progressing: adaptive-span-sample v2 reduced span counts by ~34% on p95 traffic without increasing mean latency.
- Dashboard refresh proposal ready: introduce a low-cardinality view for span cost per-route + a "span burst" heat indicator.
- Cost telemetry gap: we still have blindspot for short-lived ephemeral jobs that generate many short spans (scheduled transforms). Need short-term cap.

Standup notes (2028-02-14, 10:00am PT):
- Asha: rolled adaptive-span-sample v2 onto canary hosts (canary-ops-3/4). Observed 28–40% span reduction when prefix cache hits >= 75%. No regressions in unit tests. Follow-up: run full-A/B across traffic window on Wed. (JIRA-OBS-1284)
- Miguel: dashboard prototype for span-economics-low-card created (Grafana). Shows per-route token->span ratio and cost estimate per 1M requests. Needs annotations for quota tiers. Action: Miguel will spike annotation UX by Fri.
- Samira: investigated spike on 2028-02-11 that doubled span ingestion for ~15m. Root-cause = a batch job that started emitting a long-lived stream per item (regression in worker). Patch in review (PR #842). Rolling restart once merged.
- Jonah: telemetry pipeline lagged for 12m due to backpressure on indexing service; workaround applied (short retention buffer) but we need longer-term throttling policy.

Decisions made this week:
- Short-term: add a hard cap on per-job span emission to 10k spans/min at the agent level. This is an emergency control to keep costs bounded while we complete better sampling logic. (Mike + SRE to implement by 2028-02-17).
- Medium-term: adopt adaptive sampling as default for routes with >5k p95 spans/day with a phase rollout. Policy will be opt-out for enterprise customers initially.
- Dashboards: merge low-cardinality panel into "Traces — Overview" and add a dedicated "Span Economics" tab.

Experiments & results:
- Adaptive-span-sample v1 vs v2 (canary dataset): v1 reduced span count 18% but impacted p50 latency by ~6ms. v2 tuned to prefer prefix-KV retention and reduced p95 span count 34%, p50 latency change within noise (+1ms). Dataset: internal canary traffic, 48h window.
- Heatmap-pruning: heuristic pruning of low-signal spans (noise < 0.3) reduced ingestion by 12% but increased debugging time in a small set of cases. Next step: add "trace-tag" for pruned spans so debuggability is preserved in logs.

Open blockers:
- Missing SLA language for sampling behavior in enterprise contracts. Need legal/product input before auto-applying sampling to Dedicated customers. (Pinged Product)
- Dashboard: we need a lightweight query that doesn't explode on low-cardinality aggregate across 100k routes. Current Grafana query is O(N) and times out for large orgs. Suggestion: pre-aggregate in clickhouse pipeline. Requires infra work.

Action items (owner, due):
- Miguel: add annotations and quota tiers to span-economics-low-card dashboard (2028-02-17).
- Samira: follow up and merge worker patch to stop per-item stream leak (PR #842) + coordinate rolling restart (2028-02-15).
- Asha: run full A/B traffic test for adaptive-span-sample v2 and collect p50/p95 span ratios (2028-02-21).
- Jonah: design throttling policy for indexing service (draft doc) and propose retention buffer sizes (2028-02-20).
- SRE (assigned: Priya): implement temporary hard cap on per-job spans at agent-level (2028-02-17).

Notes to self / friction points:
- We are still measuring span->cost with a simplistic token multiplier; need to include GPU time estimate for some model-heavy routes where a single token expansion spawns many internal ops.
- Correlation between user-visible latency and span count is not linear; spike in spans sometimes correlates with more debug spans from SDK instrumentation rather than real infra issues. Need better tag hygiene.
- Consider a "safe mode" on the console that temporarily hides span-level detail when costs exceed a threshold to avoid accidental over-inspection driving SRE work.

Meeting follow-ups planned:
- Wed 11am: Asha + Miguel + Jonah — A/B results review + dashboard performance (invite sent).
- Thu 9am: Product/legal sync — sampling policy + contract language (Samira to present the impact summary).
- Fri 4pm: Open office hours for anyone to come over the canary results and dashboards (drop-in).

Quick links / refs (tickets, PRs, pages):
- JIRA-OBS-1284: adaptive-span-sample rollout plan
- JIRA-OBS-1310: dashboard low-card prototype
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/842 (worker patch)
- Playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Span+Accounting+Playbook

Raw metrics snippets (copied for posterity):
- canary window 2028-02-13 00:00 -> 2028-02-14 00:00:
  - total spans (control): 9.2M
  - total spans (v2): 6.1M
  - p95 spans/req (control): 1,320
  - p95 spans/req (v2): 890
  - mean trace ingestion latency delta: +0.9ms

TODOs (short):
- Add a column to billing export with estimated span-cost (Miguel + Billing)
- Add "pruned-span" tag in pipeline to preserve debug context for pruned spans
- Draft customer-facing note describing sampling behavior for tenants (to be reviewed by Product + Legal)

If anything urgent pops while I'm OOO next week, ping on #observability-ops and escalate to Priya or Jonah.

-- Asha
